artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n \geq 3$ without conjugate points (i.e., for every geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to M$, the Jacobi equation along $\gamma$ has no nontrivial Jacobi field vanishing at two distinct parameter values). Let $\alpha, \beta:\mathbb{R}\to M$ be two distinct unit-speed geodesics with $\alpha(0)=\beta(0)$ (so $\alpha'(0)\neq \beta'(0)$). Denote by $\mathrm{dist}_g$ the Riemannian distance on $M$.

Prove or disprove: 
$$\mathrm{dist}_g(\alpha(t),\beta(t)) \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as } t\to\infty.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The divergence of geodesics from a common basepoint in simply connected Riemannian manifolds without conjugate points is known in dimension 2 (Green, 1954) but remains open in dimensions ≥ 3; an early proof attempt was found to be flawed, and the analogous statement is known to fail in the Finsler setting (Masur, Teichmüller space).

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Holds in dimension 2 (Green, 1954); a 1956 proof is flawed; remains open in higher dimensions; fails for Finsler metrics on Teichmüller space.
status_evidence.claim: The divergence of geodesics question in manifolds without conjugate points is open in dimension ≥ 3.
